    About

    Every year since 2003 the Bureau of Labor Statistics phones thousands of Americans aged 15 and over and asks them to walk through yesterday, from 4am to 4am: what they did, for how long, where, and who was with them. About 260,000 days so far.

    This page holds 5,000 of those days, drawn in proportion to the survey's weights, so every roll is like picking one day out of all of America's days. Most of them are sleep, work, the car, the kitchen and the television. Nobody posts those.

    The days are real. The names are invented, picked from Social Security baby-name records for the year the person was born. The diaries are public and anonymous; nothing here identifies anyone. Activity labels and hashtags are ours; the timings, places and company are theirs.

    "Right now" shows what this person was doing at the time it is where you are. "True length" makes each post as tall as the time it took.

    Data: BLS American Time Use Survey · SSA baby names.
